sentenceSets.sentence: The expedition was delayed by climatic conditions that made the crossing dangerous even for experienced teams.

answerChoices.reasoning: Meteorology concerns the measurement and forecasting of the atmosphere, while the conditions here are the prevailing state of the region that makes a crossing hazardous in the first place.
'Atmospheric' points to the air itself, but the sentence describes settled conditions of the place and season that even veterans respect.
Seasonality would tie the danger to a particular time of year, whereas the sentence says only that the conditions of the region made the crossing perilous.
This near-twin word refers to a dramatic high point in a story or event, which makes no sense as a description of the conditions that delayed a crossing.
Geology concerns rock and terrain, but conditions that delay an expedition and can be waited out are not features of the ground itself.
Logistics involve supplies and transport, whereas the sentence attributes the danger to conditions the team cannot arrange around.
Nothing about permits or borders appears; the danger is to the crossing itself even for experienced teams.
Nothing in the sentence indicates a sea voyage, only a crossing made dangerous by conditions.
Money troubles would not make a crossing physically dangerous.
Ritual has nothing to do with what delayed a hazardous expedition.
Language rules cannot describe conditions on a mountain crossing.

sentenceSets.sentence: Tree rings from the valley record a long climatic shift, with wet decades giving way to a century of drought.

answerChoices.reasoning: The environment includes soil, animals, and vegetation, but the change the rings record is specifically a move from wet decades to a dry century.
Ecology concerns relationships among living things, whereas the record described here is of rainfall over long stretches of time.
Hydrology tracks water in rivers and aquifers, while the sentence describes the broader pattern of wet and dry eras that the rings preserve.
Geography concerns the arrangement of places, but nothing in the valley moved; what changed was how much rain fell over long periods.
Earthquakes are not recorded as wet decades and dry centuries in tree rings.
Human custom leaves no trace in the ring widths described here.
The trees are the instrument of the record, not its subject, which is the long swing from wet to dry.
No farming is mentioned; the rings register the rainfall itself.
A shift measured in decades and centuries is the opposite of instant.
Tree rings supply physical evidence, not invention.
Nothing in the sentence involves sound or composition.

sentenceSets.sentence: Insurers now price coastal policies with climatic projections rather than the historical loss tables they relied on for a century.

answerChoices.reasoning: Actuarial work is exactly the historical loss modeling the sentence says insurers are moving away from.
Economic forecasts concern prices and demand, but what has changed for coastal policies is the expectation of physical conditions along the shore.
Population projections would tell insurers who lives on the coast, not why the century-old loss tables no longer hold.
The loss tables being replaced are themselves statistical, so this word cannot mark the contrast the sentence draws.
New laws would change what insurers may charge, but the sentence describes a change in what they expect to happen on the coast.
Building design is not what replaced the historical tables in the pricing model.
City government is not what supplanted a century of loss tables in how these policies are priced.
A quarterly cycle describes timing, whereas the shift described is in the kind of information used.
Looking backward is precisely what the abandoned century of loss tables did.
Food has nothing to do with pricing coastal insurance.
Insurers setting real prices are not using invented figures.
